bullets.title: SNOW: +35-38% on AI monetization inflection; $6B AWS deal, guidance raised sharply
bullets.body: Snowflake surged ~35-38% pre-market on a 5%+ quarterly revenue beat ($1.39B) driven by Cortex Code AI adoption and core consumption acceleration; full-year guidance raised by $180M and cRPO accelerating q/q. Company signed a new $6B AWS commitment (~2.5x the 2023 deal) and announced OpenAI partnership expansion. Citi raises PT to $320; GS rates Buy; Wolfe All-SaaS index up 4-8% w/w on sympathy.

bullets.title: MRVL: Beat & raise with $10B+ custom silicon target by FY29; avg PT +41% to $215
bullets.body: Marvell Q1 revenue $2.42B (+0.4% beat); Q2 guide $2.70B (+3.9% above consensus); FY27 raised to $16.22B (+8.4%) and FY28 custom XPU revenue expected to more than double to $4B, targeting $10B+ by FY29. Optical Interconnect FY27 growth raised to +70% Y/Y. Sell-side average PT raised +41% to $215 (87% buy); JPM's Harlan Sur alone raised to $240 from $135. Key debate: muted beat magnitude and near-term GM headwinds from Celestial AI acquisition.

bullets.title: CRM: Agentforce ARR $1.2B (+205% YoY) but core business weakness tempers enthusiasm
bullets.body: Salesforce Q1 beat with top 10 customers spending 1.5x more YoY on AWUs; EPS beat by 24% on 135bps EBIT margin upside and $27B buyback. However, Citi's Tyler Radke cut PT to $187 (Neutral) citing Q2 guide raised only $50M vs $78M Q1 beat and deterioration in Service Cloud, Marketing/Commerce, Tableau. Raymond James reiterates Strong Buy with $290 PT (63% upside), citing Agentforce ARR +205% and 50% of bookings from existing customer expansion.

bullets.title: SNPS: Q2 beat & FY26 raised; Ansys accounting change inflated upside, debate on organic quality
bullets.body: Synopsys Q2 revenue $2.28B (+1.3% beat), EPS $3.35 (+6.3%); FY26 guidance raised to $9.625-9.705B revenue and $14.72-14.80 EPS. EDA +8% Y/Y organically, IP +12% Y/Y. Key caveat: Ansys channel revenue accounting change provided meaningful lift to Q2 upside and FY raise; beat ex-Ansys below F1Q, tempering enthusiasm. Elliott cooperation agreement noted as positive.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen teases undisclosed 'surprise product' at Computex; robotics & PC ARM chips in focus
bullets.body: Jensen Huang hinted at an unannounced Nvidia product at Computex, with speculation pointing to ARM-based laptop chips (N1/N1X) directly competing with Intel and AMD, or a dedicated robotics brain chip. MS raises TSMC 2027 CoWoS capacity estimate to 200kwpm from 160-170kwpm; Vera CPU framed as $20B opportunity. Separately, NVDA's TD Cowen conference commentary highlighted power consumption as primary data center constraint driving accelerator demand.

bullets.title: MSFT: +3% on Build Conference AI coding model announcements targeting Cursor/Claude
bullets.body: Microsoft shares rose ~3% to $425.19 after reports it will unveil a new suite of homegrown AI coding models at Build Conference, aiming to bolster GitHub Copilot against erosion from Cursor and Claude Code. Models span transcription, reasoning, speech, and image specializations. Tanium's Atlas OS also seen benefitting CRWD over MSFT/IBM in autonomous remediation.

bullets.title: META: Subscription tier launch seen as defensive; $38.5B bull case 'highly unlikely' per Oppenheimer
bullets.body: Meta launched Instagram/Facebook ($3.99/mo), WhatsApp ($2.99/mo), and Meta AI ($7.99-$49.99/mo) subscription tiers globally. Oppenheimer characterizes the move as defensive: 5% penetration (Snapchat+ benchmark) could add $8.5B or 2.8% to 2027E revenue but took Snapchat 3 years to reach. Bull case $38.5B (13% of 2027E) deemed highly unlikely. Meta AI is 3rd/4th in consumer chatbot ranking vs. ChatGPT without clear differentiation.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Cloud estimates conservative; MS raises bull case to $460; external TPU sales = $50B opportunity
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags GOOGL Cloud revenue estimates as conservative, raising bull case PT to $460 (from $425) with 77% Y/Y growth forecast for 2026 and 86% for 2027. External TPU sales could represent $50B incremental 2027 revenue. Separately, EU planning a record-breaking antitrust fine against Google with decision expected before summer recess. AAPL confirmed using NVDA privacy tech for GOOGL Cloud processing and distilling Gemini for local models.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS Bedrock driving >200bps EBIT margin expansion; Alexa for Shopping sold to 3P retailers
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes AWS Bedrock's higher-margin mix driving EBIT margin expansion >200bps q/q in 1Q26. Amazon is also selling 'Alexa for Shopping' AI technology to third-party retailers via AWS, representing a new monetization vector. SNOW's new $6B AWS commitment (~2.5x larger than 2023 deal) also signals AWS platform stickiness.

bullets.title: DELL: +3.8% on $9.7B Pentagon Microsoft license management contract
bullets.body: Dell was awarded a $9.7B US military contract for Microsoft license management, driving shares up 3.8% in pre-market. JPM hosting post-earnings call with CFO and ISG president on May 29 to discuss details. DELL is also at 52-week highs, up 176.8% YTD.

bullets.title: TTD: Initiated Sell at $11 by Rothschild Redburn on agency backlash and AI competition
bullets.body: Rothschild & Co Redburn initiated Trade Desk at Sell with $11 target, citing backlash from agencies and supply-side platforms against TTD's attempted role expansion beyond execution, plus mounting competition from media-based AI tools. TTD fell 3.1% in pre-market. Separately, Redburn initiated OMC at Neutral with $89 target on organic growth quality concerns.

bullets.title: RKT: Hedgeye adds to Best Idea Short; Quad 3 macro worst regime, -28% avg quarterly return
bullets.body: Hedgeye added Rocket Companies to its Best Idea Short list, flagging Quad 3 regime (decelerating growth + accelerating inflation) as historically the worst for RKT with -28% average quarterly returns and 0% positive batting average since IPO. CPI forecast ~4.25% in May rising to ~4.68% by year-end keeps 30Y mortgage above 6%. Revenue base effects flip negative in 3Q/4Q26 due to Redfin and Mr. Cooper acquisition anniversaries. MBA mortgage applications fell 8.5% w/w with refis down 18.1%.

bullets.title: CZR: Acquired by Fertitta Entertainment for $31/share ($17.6B total); 8% premium to prior close
bullets.body: Caesars Entertainment agreed to an all-cash acquisition by Fertitta Entertainment at $31.00/share, implying $17.6B including $11.9B assumed debt. The price is 8% above prior close and 49% above the Feb 25 baseline. Go-shop period runs through July 11. Citi maintains Neutral with $30 PT at ~7.5x 2027 EBITDA. CEO Tom Reeg expected to remain; Carano family (5% owner) rolling equity.

bullets.title: MRVL/AMD/INTC/ARM: Wolfe CPU deep-dive — AMD biggest AI CPU winner, $44B CY28 server revenue
bullets.body: Wolfe Research CPU analysis sees AMD as biggest AI CPU winner with $44B in CY28 server revenue and $7 incremental EPS (bull case $25-30 earnings power). INTC server CPU to $41.5B CY28 but only ~$1 EPS impact from AI CPU share loss. NVDA largest share winner by revenue ($25B incremental CY28) but only $0.50 incremental EPS due to scale. ARM ecosystem models 50% base case share of agentic CPU (75% upside) with ~$4.50 earnings power. TSMC wafer allocation remains main constraint.

bullets.title: AMAT: Projects >30% systems growth and >50% advanced packaging growth in 2026
bullets.body: Applied Materials at Bernstein flagged >30% systems equipment growth and >50% advanced packaging growth in 2026, with eight-quarter demand visibility. Services business growing high-teens CAGR. Data center wafer starts projected to surpass smartphone wafer starts in 2027. Inspection/measurement to exceed $1B in 2026. China business at mid-20s% of sales.

bullets.title: SNOW/PLTR/CRM AI Ghost narrative reversing: software AI monetization proving out
bullets.body: Multiple analysts noting the AI monetization skeptic narrative ('AI Ghost') is being disproved across software: Palantir first, then Datadog, now Snowflake (+34% y/y product revenue) and Salesforce Agentforce ($1.2B ARR, +205% y/y) are all showing accelerating AI-driven revenue. Cortex Code at SNOW and AWUs at CRM are the key emerging KPIs. IGV still down 11.1% YTD vs S&P +10% but multiples expanding sharply w/w.

bullets.title: HPE: Options imply ~12% move on June 1 earnings; +70% since March, Cloud & AI largest segment
bullets.body: HPE Q2 consensus is $9.78B revenue and $0.53 EPS vs guidance midpoint. Cloud & AI segment ($6.87B) is the largest contributor. Operating income guided +32-40% y/y. Stock is up 70.6% since March 9 vs S&P +10.7%. EPS beat in 16 of past 20 quarters.

bullets.title: CIEN: Up 600% Y/Y; Wolfe hosts bull/bear debate on Shannon's Limit, distributed training, margin durability
bullets.body: Ciena shares have risen over 600% Y/Y as part of the AI networking complex. Wolfe Research's bull/bear debate (May 22 replay available) examines distributed training as key growth driver, multi-rail amplifier TAM, Coherent Lite timing, pluggable risk to the business, and long-term margin/EPS power. Supply chain constraints also a concern at current growth rates.

bullets.title: FSLR/ENPH: Solar stocks technical breakout on tariff escalation; FSLR +7.5% day, +89% YTD
bullets.body: Solar stocks are showing major technical breakouts amid tariff escalation discussion. FSLR is up 7.5% on the session and 88.9% YTD, triggering 52-week high watchlist alerts. ENPH also flagged in the solar breakout narrative.

bullets.title: DKNG: Kalshi sports betting handle +12% W/W; NBA Conference Finals driving +47% NBA handle
bullets.body: Hedgeye sports betting tracker shows Kalshi handle up 12% week-over-week with NBA Conference Finals driving +47% NBA handle and MLB +31%. Goldman's DKS upgrade note also cites 2026 FIFA World Cup (June 11-July 19) as a potential $17B GDP-impact event with meaningful upside for media/ad beneficiaries including FOXA.
